newsitem.title: CHINA: HK leader Tung appoints handler for Taiwan ties.
newsitem.headline: HK leader Tung appoints handler for Taiwan ties.

text.p: Hong Kong's leader Tung Chee-hwa has appointed a member of his inner advisory cabinet to act as his intermediary on Taiwan-Hong Kong relations, Taiwan's representative in the territory Koo Chen-fu said on Thursday.
"Mr Tung specially said matters between the two places will be undertaken by Mr Paul Yip...and Cheng An-kuo," Koo told a news conference after meeting Tung for half an hour of talks.
Koo is in charge of an intermediary body that Taipei authorises to handle relations with the communist mainland.

Yip is a member of Tung's Executive Council and Cheng heads Taipei's unofficial mission in Hong Kong, the Chung Hwa Travel Agency. "The two will talk and manage (Hong Kong Taiwan affairs)," said Koo, who was accompanied by Cheng.
"Mr Tung has said that Mr Yip will discuss further with me on Taiwan-Hong Kong matters," Cheng said. "Mr Yip will represent the Hong Kong Government," he said.
"We hope Taiwan-Hong Kong relations will be even more intimate, smooth...to build a more complete, normal, stable Hong Kong-Taiwan relationship.
Cheng confirmed the Chung Hwa Travel Agency would remain Taipei's representative office in Hong Kong for the time being.
Speculation on Taiwan's status in Hong Kong after the former British colony reverted to China this week has been intense.
Tung said on Wednesday he expected to settle the status of Taiwan-Hong Kong relations quickly.
Beijing views Taiwan as a renegade province destined for reunification with the mainland under the same "one country, two systems" formula applied in Hong Kong.
Tung's spokesman declined to give details of the talks.
